earnings.title: Agilent Reports Fourth-Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results
highlights: Revenue of $2.04 billion for the fourth quarter ended Oct. 31, 2026, representing growth of 9.6% reported and up 8.3% core (1) compared with the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.
GAAP net income of $451 million; earnings per share (EPS) of $1.59, an increase of 4% from the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Non-GAAP net income (3) of $526 million (including a $20 million net benefit from tariff refunds); non-GAAP EPS (3) of $1.86 (including a $0.07 net benefit from tariff refunds), an increase of 17% from the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.
Revenue of $7.55 billion for the fiscal year ended Oct. 31, 2026, representing growth of 8.7% reported and up 6.6% core (1) compared with fiscal year 2025.
GAAP operating margin of 25.0%, expanded by 120 basis points year-over-year and 140 basis points sequentially.

quotes.text: We closed FY26 well ahead of our initial outlook, with momentum building quarter by quarter and robust growth across all our end markets, driven by our strong execution and the compounding benefits of the Ignite Operating System on both the top and bottom lines.

outlook: Fiscal year 2027 revenue is expected in the range of $8.00 billion to $8.15 billion, representing a range of up 6.0% to 8.0% reported and up 5.0% to 7.0% core (1)(5) .

Excluding the net benefit of tariff refunds recognized in fiscal year 2026, non-GAAP fiscal year 2027 operating margin expansion (2) at the midpoint of core revenue guidance is expected to be approximately 70 basis points higher relative to 26.8% in fiscal year 2026.

Non-GAAP fiscal year 2027 EPS (4) is expected in the range of $6.73 to $6.86, an increase of 7.3% at the midpoint compared with non-GAAP fiscal year 2026 EPS of $6.34, which included the net benefit of tariff refunds.
Excluding the net benefit of tariff refunds recognized in fiscal year 2026, EPS growth is expected to be 8.5% to 10.5%.

items.heading: General economic conditions may adversely affect our operating results and financial condition.
Our operating results and financial condition could be harmed if the markets into which we sell our products decline or do not grow as anticipated.
Economic, political, foreign currency and other risks associated with international sales and operations could adversely affect our results of operations.

If we do not introduce successful new products and services in a timely manner to address increased competition through frequent new product and service introductions, rapid technological changes and changing industry standards, our products and services may become obsolete, and our operating results may suffer.
Demand for some of our products and services depends on the capital spending policies of our customers, research and development budgets and on government funding policies.
Recent and dynamic government rule making and policy changes could increase our costs, affect our markets and customers and impact our results of operations.
